glosses: To draw in the breath suddenly, as if from a shock.

examples.text: The audience gasped as the magician disappeared.

glosses: To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion; to respire with heaving of the breast; to pant.

examples.text: We were all gasping when we reached the summit.

c. 1761-1764, Robert Lloyd, An Epistle to C. Churchill, Author of the Rosicad
She gasps and struggles hard for life.

glosses: To speak in a breathless manner.

examples.text: The old man gasped his last few words.

glosses: To pant with eagerness or excitement; to show vehement desire.

examples.text: I'm gasping for a cup of tea.
Quenching the gasping furrows' thirst with rain.

glosses: A short, sudden intake of breath.

examples.text: The audience gave a gasp of astonishment

glosses: A draw or drag on a cigarette (or gasper).

examples.text: I'm popping out for a gasp.

glosses: The sound of a gasp.

examples.text: Gasp! What will happen next?

glosses: A quick breathing; a catching of the breath; a gasp: the panting of animals such as a dog with their tong hung out- as a form of thermoregulation.
Eager longing.

examples.text: Indeed, the projections, cravings, and everyday frolics common to trysts among buzz-activist Hollywood stars and starlets, plus their many common folk imitators, go forward with eager pant.

glosses: A violent palpitation of the heart.

examples.text: To this great fairy I'll commend thy acts, / Make her thanks bless thee. O thou day o' the world, / Chain mine arm'd neck; leap thou, attire and all; / Through proof of harness to my heart, and there / Ride on the pants triumphing.

glosses: To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion or from eagerness or excitement; to respire with heaving of the breast; to gasp.

examples.text: Pluto pants for breath from out his cell.
There is a cavern where my spirit / Was panted forth in anguish.

glosses: To long eagerly; to desire earnestly.

examples.text: As the hart panteth after the water brooks.

glosses: To long for (something); to be eager for (something).

examples.text: Then shall our hearts pant thee.

glosses: Of the heart, to beat with unnatural violence or rapidity; to palpitate.

examples.text: Yet might her piteous heart be seen to pant and quake

glosses: To sigh; to flutter; to languish.
